paper.title_en: 1+1 dimensional relativistic viscous magnetohydrodynamics with self-consistent longitudinal acceleration
paper.abstract_en: We study $(1+1)$-dimensional relativistic viscous magnetohydrodynamics with self-consistent longitudinal acceleration under the conformal equation of state $\varepsilon=3p$. We evolve temperature, fluid rapidity, and shear stress using energy conservation, longitudinal momentum conservation, and a shear-relaxation law in a prescribed transverse magnetic stress. Moving beyond longitudinal boost invariance, we derive perturbative analytical expressions in the Navier--Stokes approximation and obtain nonlinear solutions with shear relaxation, comparing dynamical and prescribed accelerating flows from identical initial conditions. The initial temperature curvature generates a longitudinal pressure gradient that alters the rapidity slope, modifies longitudinal expansion work, and produces a distinct cooling history. For the reference parameters, shear viscosity enhances the resulting central temperature difference much more strongly than the prescribed magnetic stress, while the condition for equal central temperatures shifts with proper time and initial shear. At $χ=λ^*=0.03$, the maximum relative difference in central temperature is $0.18\%$ over $0.6$--$6$~fm/$c$, despite a persistent momentum residual in the prescribed flow. Because the velocity mapping also enters the entropy per unit fluid rapidity, the rapidity distribution remains sensitive to the flow evolution even when central temperatures closely agree. Replacing the prescribed field with ideal induction removes direct magnetic work while retaining magnetic pressure and inertia in the longitudinal momentum balance.
